supporting_evidence: Localization-failure objects were smaller than TP objects: median min-side 8 vs 10 px and median area 78.5 vs 108 px²; 192→640 crops raised the overall median represented min-side to 33.3 px and the small+low-contrast median to 26.7 px; a 25% overlapped 192 grid fully contained 100% of GT boxes in this simulation.
conflicting_evidence: All FN combined had a min-side median of 9 px versus 10 px for TP and the component-bootstrap median difference CI crossed zero (-2 to 3 px); low-confidence FN were larger rather than smaller (median 13 px); crop analysis assumes an oracle/grid patch contains the object and is not detector evidence.
expected_benefit: May improve spatial representation and localization of the smallest objects, especially localization failures.
risk: More patches increase inference cost and duplicate predictions; boundary handling/NMS are required; object-centric crop values are upper-bound feasibility rather than deployable proposal performance.
decision: Test one leakage-safe 192 px patch strategy with 25% overlap before broader search; retain full-image baseline as comparator.

supporting_evidence: Localization failures had lower absolute median contrast than TP (3 vs 8; bootstrap median-difference CI -5.25 to -1). Mild CLAHE raised median absolute contrast by 5 overall and by 2 in the small+low-contrast subgroup; mild bilateral filtering raised small+low-contrast robust CNR-like proxy by 0.067 while keeping median bbox intensity correlation at 0.978.
conflicting_evidence: CLAHE reduced median robust CNR-like proxy by 0.045 in the small+low-contrast subgroup and amplified background gradient to 1.759×; low-confidence FN already had higher contrast than TP; feature changes do not prove detector improvement. Gaussian-reference feature gains conflict with the negative B6 detector experiment and are not promoted.
expected_benefit: A conservative visibility transform may help low-contrast localization cases if background amplification is controlled.
risk: Enhancement can amplify background/artifact traces or alter tiny structures; method choice may trade contrast against noise.
decision: Prioritize mild bilateral/edge-preserving input as a single controlled ablation; CLAHE is secondary and requires explicit background-amplification monitoring.

supporting_evidence: The pre-specified small+low-contrast subgroup had 10 FN among 101 objects (recall 0.9010), below small-only 0.9742, low-contrast-only 0.9903, and neither 0.9721. With 192→640 crops, its median min-side became 26.7 px; CLAHE improved contrast in 84.2% and bilateral in 46.5% of subgroup objects. The joint 192-crop≥24 px plus contrast-improvement coverage was 46.5% for CLAHE and 26.7% for bilateral.
conflicting_evidence: Projected joint benefit is feature-level only; CLAHE increased background gradient about 1.759× and its median CNR-like change was negative; combining interventions can interact adversely, as earlier B3 showed for a different augmentation combination.
expected_benefit: Directly targets the strongest observed B0 interaction and may combine localization-scale and visibility benefits.
risk: Highest complexity and attribution ambiguity; patch duplicates, compute, and enhancement artifacts must be controlled; combined testing should follow single-axis experiments.
decision: Justified only after separate scale and visibility ablations; do not start with the combined pipeline.
